backdown remote

Other machines (a NAS, another computer) whose BackDown index is read over ssh, so copies there count for duplicates and wiping (Pro).

On this page
  • backdown remote add
  • Arguments
  • Options
  • backdown remote list
  • Options
  • backdown remote remove
  • Arguments
  • backdown remote sync
  • Arguments
  • backdown remote test
  • Arguments
  • backdown remote settings
  • Options
  • Good to know
  • Examples
  • See also
backdown remote [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

backdown remote add#

Add a machine whose BackDown index is read over ssh (with your keys; never a password)

backdown remote add [OPTIONS] <NAME> <URL>

Arguments#

<NAME>
What to call it, like nas or office-pc.
<URL>
ssh://[user@]host[:port] (a host alias from ~/.ssh/config works too).

Options#

--remote-db <PATH> next preview
Its index there, if not its default (or the one its BackDown service uses). (The global --db is this machine's index).
--backdown <PATH>
Where backdown is there, if not on the PATH ssh sessions get.
--no-test next preview
Don't try to reach it now.

backdown remote list#

The machines, their drives, and when they were last synced.

backdown remote list [OPTIONS]

Options#

--json
Print it as JSON, for scripts.

backdown remote remove#

Forget a machine and what was cached about it (nothing there is touched)

backdown remote remove [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments#

<NAME>
A machine's name from backdown remote list.

backdown remote sync#

Fetch what changed in a machine's index (all of them without NAME); files there whose size matches a file here are hashed there, so copies can be proved.

backdown remote sync [OPTIONS] [NAME]

Arguments#

[NAME]
A machine's name from backdown remote list. Without it, every machine.

backdown remote test#

Try reaching a machine: ssh, BackDown there, its index.

backdown remote test [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments#

<NAME>
A machine's name from backdown remote list.

backdown remote settings#

How long a copy on another machine counts as proof after it was last confirmed there, and how often machines are synced.

backdown remote settings [OPTIONS]

Options#

--proof-days <PROOF_DAYS>
Days (1–90; 7 unless changed).
--sync-hours <SYNC_HOURS> next preview
Hours between syncs (6 unless changed).

All of them also take the global options --db and --local.

Good to know#

The other machine needs BackDown installed and an index. BackDown runs your system's ssh as you, with BatchMode=yes (never a password) and your known hosts, and starts backdown serve-stdio there, which only reads its index and hashes a file only when asked; nothing listens on the network, and no file's contents are sent. A copy there counts only by SHA-256, and only when confirmed there within the proof window (7 days unless changed). The background service syncs each machine every 6 hours. add, test and sync need Pro (unlocked in pre-release versions); list and remove don't. Windows machines can't be the other end yet.

Examples#

backdown remote add nas ssh://you@nas.example.org
# BackDown isn't on the PATH ssh sessions get there
backdown remote add office ssh://office-pc --backdown /opt/backdown/backdown
backdown remote test nas
backdown remote sync
backdown remote list
# copies there count for 14 days after they were last confirmed there
backdown remote settings --proof-days 14
backdown remote remove nas

  • Several machines
